text:
Unai Emery has insisted he will not alter his plans for Aston Villa’s Champions Leaguegame at Galatasaray on Tuesday night on account of concerns about the state of the pitch. The Turkish champions hastily moved Saturday’s home fixture from Rams Park after starting emergency repairs to the surface this month. The Villa defender Ian Maatsen said he and his teammates were aware the pitch was in a “bad condition”.
Villa were informed by Uefa last week that they would be unable to train at the venue the day before the Champions League game in order to give the pitch maximum time to recover after heavy maintenance work. Galatasaray played Saturday’s victory over Samsunspor at Basaksehir Fatih Terim stadium, a significantly smaller ground named after the former Turkey manager, who played for and managed Galatasaray.
Galatasaray’s manager, Okan Buruk, acknowledged the pitch would pose problems despite round-the-clock efforts to improve the hybrid surface, where sand remains present. “We are not expecting a perfect pitch, but we are at least expecting a pitch that will be playable and will not get any worse or deteriorate during the game,” he said.
Villa instead trained at Bodymoor Heath, their Warwickshire base, on Monday before flying to Istanbul. Villa typically choose to train there before flying to games overseas, though they trained at Fenerbahce on the eve of their Europa League visit in January, and at Besiktas Park 24 hours before their Europa League triumph in Istanbul in May.
“If we could have trained in the stadium of Galatasaray, maybe we would have decided for the same situation, but it’s not changing our routine,” Emery said. “How the pitch is going to be tomorrow is important, but it’s not an excuse because it’s [the same] for both teams. Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible.”
The Villa manager added: “If the pitch was not available or a risk for the players, for some injuries, we are not playing there. I think it’s going to be [good] enough, well enough to play the match. We are thinking only to face them [Galatasaray] and thinking only to play how we are, not changing our idea or our plan for the pitch.”
Victor Osimhen is sidelined for Galatasaray with a knee injury, but the record 26-time Turkish champions expect to welcome back the former Tottenham defender Davinson Sánchez. The former Arsenal midfielder Lucas Torreira and Yunus Akgun, who spent 2023-24 on loan at Leicester, scored in the 2-1 win over Samsunspor, which maintained their three-point lead in the Super Lig.
Buruk was sent off after full-time, after receiving a second yellow card for failing to shake hands with the referee, Ali Sansalan, but his touchline ban does not apply to the Champions League. Galatasaray have appealed to the Turkish Football Federation against the dismissal.
“You can shake hands if you want, or not,” Buruk said. “As long as you don’t show disrespect or use abusive language, no one can punish anyone. The referee made a mistake. I expect that mistake to be reversed.”
